items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In fact, that's where I first met Bob Mitchell, the trumpet player with Jimmie Lunceford; I met him there.

ctx.x: -- we had to rehearse the production. So I had to make a decision. I said, 'Well, now, I'm going to be a musician, that's for sure, so I just want to stay on this job' -- because it was the best job in Detroit at the time, you know. So I gave up school in Eleventh Grade. I gave it up. I haven't really regretted it. In fact, my high school principal, Mister Sanders, back in Jackson at Lanier High School, he wrote me a letter and told me to just come back and go through the graduation exercises, you know, he said…

This band was pretty much like a family. In fact, quite a few nights...practically every night after we finished work, we would go down on the corner to a place where we would eat breakfast and sit around and rap, and the other musicians would come...called cookers(?). The other musicians would drop by. In fact, that's where I first met Bob Mitchell, the trumpet player with Jimmie Lunceford; I met him there. I met a lot of nice fellows that used to come through there and hang every night. And then we would leave…
